newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saint-Louis sees better H2 for paper.
newsitem.headline: Saint-Louis sees better H2 for paper.

text.p: Saint-Louis forecast on Wednesday better earnings for its paper unit Arjo Wiggins Appleton in the second half of the year.

In a statement, Saint-Louis said earnings prospects for Arjo Wiggins Appleton were "more favourable," citing an improvement in the production capacity usage rate at the end of the first half of 1996 as orders picked up.
The forecast also assumed modest economic growth in Europe and satisfactory growth in the United States, it said.
The paper branch reported a fall in net profit before exceptionals to 79 million francs in the first half of 1996 from 296 million francs in the same period for 1995.
The performance of the agro-food sector was "in line with our expectations" and the sector should show "satisfactory results" in the second half, the statement said.
Saint-Louis also announced that before end of the year it would control the 65,000 tonne sugar quota belonging to the Marle refinery.
The acquisition results from the resale by Eridania Beghin-Say to Saint-Louis and other sugar producers of some of the assets of Compagnie Francaise de Sucrerie.
Saint-Louis also confirmed it would sell its 34.5 percent in processed food unit Panzalim to Danone before the end of the year.
Danone, which held a majority in Panzalim, has already announced plans to acquire the Panzalim stake.
Saint-Louis also confirmed plans to link up its mushroom business with that of the Champi-Jandou cooperative in a venture operated by Champi-Jandou.
